description: Media stack: VPN egress for torrents, qBittorrent, the *arr apps, and the resources behind them.

panels.title: VPN (torrent egress must never leave the tunnel)
Tunnel
panels.description: gluetun_up: 1 when the VPN has a public IP. If this is 0 the kill-switch and the qbittorrent-egress NetworkPolicy are the only things stopping traffic - both hold, but nothing will be downloading either.

panels.title: Exit IP
panels.description: Must be the VPN provider's address. If this ever shows the home Telekom IP, torrent traffic is leaking - treat as an incident.

panels.title: Forwarded port
panels.description: 0 means the provider gave us no forwarded port, which silently kills inbound peer connections - downloads slow to a crawl with no error anywhere.

panels.title: Stalled
panels.description: stalledDL means the torrent is active but no peer is serving it - usually a dead torrent with zero seeders, not a fault.

panels.title: DHT nodes
panels.description: Peer-discovery reach. A collapse here usually means the tunnel or the forwarded port broke.

panels.title: Torrents by state
panels.description: Zero-valued states are filtered out so the legend stays readable.

panels.title: Health issues reported by each app
panels.description: These are the same warnings the apps show in their own UI (indexer errors, download-client failures, root-folder problems).

panels.title: Free space on the media root folders
panels.description: These all sit on the same NFS export from the NAS (ZFS), so they move together. ZFS write performance degrades well before a pool is full - watch the trend, not just the number.

panels.title: CPU by pod
panels.description: Jellyfin dominating this is normal - it is the only thing that transcodes.

panels.title: Container restarts
panels.description: Cumulative - a step up is a restart.

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: Every exporter feeding this dashboard. A 0 here means the panels above are stale, so read this before trusting them.

panels.title: Jellyfin .NET heap
panels.description: Jellyfin's built-in metrics are .NET runtime only - it exposes no stream or transcode counts, so this is the extent of what it gives us without a separate API exporter.

panels.title: Jellyfin reachable
panels.description: 1 = the exporter reached the Jellyfin API on its last scrape.

panels.title: Streaming now
panels.description: Active playback sessions right now. 0 is normal when nobody is watching - the now-playing series only exist during playback.

panels.title: Users streaming
panels.description: Distinct users with something playing right now.

panels.title: Accounts
panels.description: Total Jellyfin accounts (includes the media-e2e test account).

panels.title: Active in last 7d
panels.description: Accounts that carry a last_access timestamp.

panels.title: Transcoding now
panels.description: Sessions whose playback method is a transcode - these are the CPU-expensive ones.

panels.title: Pending restart
panels.description: Jellyfin is waiting for a restart to finish applying a change.

panels.title: Collectors failing
panels.description: Any value above 0 means part of this dashboard is blind - check the exporter's auth.

panels.title: Library growth
panels.description: How the library has grown. Flat lines are normal for types you do not collect.

panels.title: Playing right now
panels.description: Empty when nobody is watching. Shows who is watching what, on which device, and whether it is being transcoded.

panels.title: Most watched (approx. watch time, by title)
panels.description: Approximate: the exporter is scraped every 5 minutes, so each observation of a title in a playing state counts as 5 minutes. Short views can be missed entirely and totals are rounded to 5-minute steps - good for ranking what gets watched, not for exact hours. Fills in as the library is used; empty right after deployment.

panels.title: Watch time by user (approx.)
panels.description: Same 5-minute sampling caveat as Most watched - use it for comparing users, not for exact totals.

panels.title: Accounts
panels.description: Every Jellyfin account. admin=1 marks administrators; last_access is a unix timestamp.
